scripts.//-- setup --: One-time bootstrap: install deps, start local Postgres (:5434), apply migrations, start Mailpit (:8026) and MinIO (:9002, PDF reports). See docs/run-locally.md.
scripts.setup: pnpm install && pnpm dev:db:up && pnpm dev:db:migrate && pnpm dev:mail:up && pnpm dev:s3:up
scripts.//-- dev --: dev = frontend (:7777) + backend (:3001) in parallel. Needs dev:db:up first. The background-job worker is opt-in: dev:full = dev + the worker, or dev:run:worker on its own (JOB_TRANSPORT=inprocess: polls the job table every 15 s and wakes on LISTEN job_queued; Postgres only, no AWS). dev:jobs:tick runs one tick (every due job) and exits. dev:feeds:run is one tick that first queues every enabled data feed, due or not (FEED_SOURCE=fixtures by default: synthetic files, no network). dev:ingest:push posts the synthetic logger CSV (scripts/ingest/fixture.csv, re-dated to end yesterday) to the ingest endpoint with the API key in WM_INGEST_KEY (env or the gitignored root .env.development.local; make the key under Settings → API keys). See docs/run-locally.md § Background jobs, § Data feeds and § Ingest.
scripts.//-- db --: Local Postgres 17 in docker on :5434 (user/db water, app role water_app). Migrations live in backend/migrations.
scripts.dev:db:reset: docker compose down -v && pnpm dev:db:up && pnpm dev:db:migrate
scripts.//-- mail --: Mailpit catches all local email (verify, password reset, invites, alerts): SMTP :1026, web UI http://localhost:8026. The backend's dev default is MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp → Mailpit; see docs/run-locally.md § Email. dev:mail:bounce <email> [--complaint | --transient] stands in for SES's bounce and complaint events (no SES locally): it flags that account's address as suppressed, pausing its alert emails behind the banner on the account and alert pages (needs dev:db:up; docs/run-locally.md § Alerts).
scripts.//-- s3 --: MinIO: S3-compatible storage for server-side PDF reports (STORAGE=local, the default): API :9002, console http://localhost:9003 (minioadmin / minioadmin, dev-only). The backend creates the water-reports bucket on first use. The worker renders reports with the Chromium from test:e2e:install; see docs/run-locally.md § Reports.
scripts.//-- data --: Demo data. seed:examples = 3 invented catchments (skipped once they exist) + 2 demo users (demo@ / analyst@example.com) + 2 demo farmers (farmer1@ / farmer2@example.com) + a demo applicant with a submitted application (applicant@example.com), password demo-password, works on any clone. seed:demo = seed:examples + each client workbook in ../project-water-management-source/Original/ (WBT_SOURCE_DIR) as its own project, named from its file name at run time, skipping any the demo user already has (needs Python + openpyxl, scripts/wbt-import/README.md); a workbook's gauge column is imported as a reference gauge, with per-workbook settings in wbt-import.<prefix>.env beside the workbooks (bin/seed-demo.sh; WBT_SETTINGS / WBT_FIT=1 patch the settings and fit GR4J at import, docs/model.md §2.10b). pan-sensitivity takes any project.json (no DB): GR4J at a few pan-coefficient choices, fixed vs refitted, written to a Markdown table (docs/model.md §2.4a). fit-sweep <project.json> --grid <grid.json> fits GR4J once per cell of a grid of fit settings (pan preset × bounds × objective × named exclusion set × WR2012 band on/off), with validation, and writes one Markdown table (and --json), ranking nothing (no DB; at most 24 cells unless --max-cells; docs/model.md §2.10b). Both resolve paths from where you typed the command; a report on the client catchment stays in the gitignored data/client-catchment/, never committed.
scripts.//-- gen --: Generated assets, committed. gen:help-art renders the help pictures (one Blender scene, several shots) with Blender 5 + ImageMagick 7 (optional tooling; scripts/help-art/catchment.py; HELP_ART_ONLY=shot,… for some). gen:landing-art regenerates everything the public landing page shows (issue #57, docs/design/landing-art.md): the diorama lit for day and dusk (Blender, the help scene), contours, icons and device frames (Inkscape), AVIF/WebP and the social card (ImageMagick, avifenc, FontForge), the app screens (Playwright on the example catchments; needs dev:db:up) and the charts and what-if grid (the engine); optional tooling, LANDING_ART_ONLY=render,vector,screens,data for some steps, LANDING_ART_DEVICE for the GPU. gen:limitations rewrites packages/engine/src/liability/limitations.generated.ts from docs/engine-audit.md (the open audit items a validation statement and a sign-off list, WP-3.13); its test fails until you rerun it after changing an audit item. gen:i18n:sheet [lang…] rewrites docs/i18n/<code>-translation-sheet.md, the strings a farmer sees that have no reviewed words yet in that language, read from the frontend's t() / msg() / plural() calls (WP-2.5; docs/ui.md § Language), and frontend/src/lib/i18n/messages/ids.generated.ts, every message's id (default: every non-English language in packages/engine/src/languages.ts); rerun it after adding or changing a message or a translation. gen:i18n:stamp <lang> <id> re-stamps a farmer glossary translation's sourceHash from the current English once the translator has re-checked it (and rewrites that language's sheet). gen:i18n:export <lang> <dir> writes that language's sheet rows as JSON batches for translation (the i18n-translator agent, .claude/agents/i18n/); gen:i18n:apply <lang> <id→words.json …> checks returned translations (placeholders, bold, whole plurals and glossary entries) and writes them into that language's three catalogues (creating one that doesn't exist yet), then rewrites its sheet.
scripts.//-- build --: Production builds: static frontend (frontend/build) and the Lambda bundle (backend/dist/lambda.mjs).
scripts.//-- check --: Typecheck every workspace, plus the repo guards CI runs: committed env files stay local (check:env), the Claude agents and commands cite only real paths and no template placeholders (check:claude), workflow pins/OIDC/gate rules + actionlint (check:workflows), frontend bundle ceilings (check:bundle, after build:frontend), advisory privacy-doc drift vs origin/main (check:compliance), no client-identifying term in any tracked file or path (check:terms; needs ../infra-secrets/water-management/client-terms.txt, else a no-op), every language's translation sheet is current and no glossary translation is stale (check:i18n lists what is untranslated or stale, for every language; fix with gen:i18n:sheet / gen:i18n:stamp <lang> <id>). The five Playwright pins agree and are exact (check:pins: backend and renderer-deps playwright-core, its lockfile, e2e's @playwright/test, the renderer image tag; plus the renderer image's base digest and its apt packages at exact versions from one snapshot; scripts/guards/check_playwright_pins.mjs). check:workflows also keeps github_actions and docker off the Dependabot auto-merge allowlist, and the renderer image's npm directory (/backend/renderer-deps) out of auto-merge.
scripts.//-- test --: test:changed = the fast inner loop: typecheck + vitest --changed for only what the working changes touch (seconds; db tests too when :5434 is up; never e2e), see docs/testing.md. test = unit tests everywhere (no DB, no wall-clock assertions; the gate before a commit). test:guards = node:test suites for the CI/release guards in scripts/ and the infra scripts (infra/scripts/restore-db.sh against a fake aws + terraform; needs bash and jq). test:backend:db needs dev:db:up; it migrates and uses the water_test database (water_test_w<n> in a git worktree, backend/src/__tests__/test-db.ts). test:engine:perf / test:backend:perf are separate performance-budget targets (median of several runs; not part of `test` because a busy machine or parallel workspaces would make a hard wall-clock ceiling flake — run them alone). test:backend:perf:db is the same for budgets that need Postgres (dev:db:up; it rebuilds the checkout's water_test… like test:backend:db, so never beside it); not in CI either.
scripts.//-- e2e --: Playwright (Chromium), fully local. Needs dev:db:up; rebuilds its own database and starts its own backend + a production build of the frontend (frontend/build-e2e; dev servers and frontend/build untouched): water_e2e, :3101 and :7801 in the main checkout, a per-worktree slot elsewhere (E2E_SLOT overrides; e2e/support/env.ts), so two checkouts can run it at once. First time: test:e2e:install. See e2e/README.md.
scripts.//-- infra --: Terraform in infra/: credential-free fmt -check + validate + plan-only `terraform test` (mocked providers, tests/guardrails.tftest.hcl). Needs terraform (tfenv, infra/.terraform-version). Never plans against or applies to AWS; see infra/README.md.
scripts.//-- renderer --: The report renderer's container image (backend/renderer.Dockerfile, the release path's image): check:renderer-image packages the Lambdas, builds the image and smoke-tests it as Lambda runs it (Chromium prints a PDF; the handler answers under the Lambda runtime interface emulator, pinned in infra/scripts/smoke-renderer-image.sh; the init check refuses a missing setting). Needs docker; no AWS account; ~3.5 GB image. CI runs the same (ci.yml, renderer-image); see docs/deployment.md § Reports. Its build stage's apt packages are pinned to one Ubuntu archive snapshot (APT_SNAPSHOT) that nothing moves by itself: check:apt-snapshot says how old it is (limit 90 days; renderer-apt-snapshot.yml runs it weekly and opens an issue when stale), and gen:renderer-apt [<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ>] moves it (default today) and rewrites every pinned version to its candidate in that snapshot, read with apt-cache in the Dockerfile's digest-pinned base (docker run, no build; needs network). Run gen:renderer-apt whenever the base digest moves (Dependabot's docker PR), then check:pins and check:renderer-image. scripts/guards/renderer_apt_snapshot.mjs.
